title: On a screenshot, a drawing tool says where its first point will land too
goal: With the grid on, a ring now shows where a press would put the first point of a shape. On a plain screenshot with no grid, the same tools still quietly pull that first point onto a border they found in the picture, and you only find out after you press. Give the screenshot case the same ring the grid case has.
notes:
Split out of the-grid-line-under-a-pen-point-lights-up-while on 2026-09-15. The mark there is deliberately gated on the grid pulling, and this is the half that gate leaves out.

The blocker is cost, and it is measured. Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/DrawLandingCostTests.swift, run with `swift test --filter DrawLandingCostTests`, prints:

  [perf] a grid and twenty guides, nothing photographed: 5.9 us a mouse move
  [perf] the Pen with forty anchors down: 0.5 us a mouse move
  [perf] grid over a 2560x1600 screenshot, 104 borders in it: 2530.2 us a mouse move
  [perf] the same screenshot with only four borders in it: 2390.3 us a mouse move

So one AnnotationSnapping.snap over a big picture costs about 2.4ms, and the last two lines are the finding: the cost is the picture WIDTH, not what is drawn on it. EdgeMap.verticalEdges/horizontalEdges allocate a [Double] the full width (or height) of the picture and sum every block row into it on every call, then refinedPeaks scans the whole profile. Nothing is cached between calls.

This is a pre-existing hot path rather than anything new: snapMeasureAnchor pays it on every measure hover move today, and snappedAnnotationPoint pays it on every mouseDragged frame while an arrow is drawn on a screenshot. No user-visible jank has been reproduced from it, which is why this is p2 and not p1 - it is a number, not a complaint. Making it cheap (a cached profile per picture, or a windowed scan instead of a full-width one) would let the hover mark cover screenshots and would take the cost off the drag path at the same time.
acceptance: Hovering with the arrow, rectangle or line tool over a screenshot, with no grid on, shows the mark on the border the press would actually land on
The mark is absent when no border is near enough to catch, so it never sits under the pointer saying nothing
One hover frame costs under 200 microseconds on a 2560 by 1600 screenshot, measured and reported
Drawing a shape across that same screenshot is no slower than it is today
